cine.caption1: By 2189 nobody is just human any more. Six alien lineages married into ours, and the group chats have never been worse.
cine.caption2: Six friends on a tourist liner, and not one parent on board.

cine.line1: Imagine if we actually find aliens.
cine.line2: Bro. Look at us. We are the aliens.
cine.line3: The centre of the galaxy, with you lot. This trip is giving main character energy.
cine.montage: Day 41: beyond the edge of charted space
cine.line5: That reading is impossible. Gravity doesn't do that.
cine.ai1: WARNING. UNIDENTIFIED GRAVITATIONAL DISTURBANCE DETECTED. NAVIGATION SYSTEMS EXPERIENCING ANOMALOUS DEVIATION.

wake.line1: Ow. Okay. Either I'm dead, or this is a one-star stay on Trapadvisor.
wake.line2: Two worlds in the sky. That is not our Moon. That's nobody's Moon.
wake.line3: Hello? Squad? {f:social}? {f:strong}? And the device just died. Bro, even the group chat is dead.
wake.line4: Something is moving between the trees. Something huge. Nope. Nope nope nope.
wake.line5: Stay calm. Think like a scientist. Scientists drink water. Step one: don't die.

fruit.examineRed: Hard thorns and an oily red skin. Your fingers tingle where you touched it. Bad idea.
fruit.ateBlue: Sweet and strange: like pear and pepper. Your body accepts it.

crew.scientist.name: Zenvik
crew.scientist.line: {lin}. Two doctorates. Can explain a black hole, cannot open a jar.
crew.strong.name: Draxum
crew.strong.line: Korrath-human from the foundries of Titan. Claims three hundred aura points. Cries at adverts and will deny it.
crew.medic.name: Lyrra
crew.medic.line: Vael-human from the garden domes of Mars. Has never raised her voice. Her sarcasm has a licence.
crew.explorer.name: Skyvra
crew.explorer.line: Tarnkin-human from the ice caravans of Ganymede. Always on a side quest. Keeps a ledger of who owes her snacks.
crew.builder.name: Bolzar
crew.builder.line: Ortek-human from the shipyards of Ceres. Says everything he builds will hold. Allegedly.
crew.social.name: Nuvexa
crew.social.line: Sirelle-human from the cloud cities of Venus. Forty million followers and one real friend group.
level.4.desc: Night is coming. Gather dry moss for tinder, build a fire pit at your camp and strike stones until a spark catches.
level.4.hint: Your camp site glows near the wreck. Dry moss grows in the open clearing.
level.5.desc: Cut giant fronds and gather branches, then build a lean-to beside the fire.
level.5.hint: Giant fronds grow at the edge of the forest.
level.6.desc: Something hunts here at night. Lash a flint point to a straight branch with glowvine.
level.6.hint: Flint shards lie among the rocks; glowvine coils on the ground under the trees.
level.7.desc: Rest at the shelter until dark. When night falls, hold the camp until dawn: keep the fire fed from the wood pile beside it, guard the food, and set traps while you still can. Then sleep.
level.7.hint: A fed fire keeps them back. When it burns low, go to it and press [[interact]].
level.8.desc: Eat first: spear a fish in the shallows or hunt in the meadow. Your wrist device has also picked up a crew signal, too weak to locate. After breakfast, climb to the crystal ridge and tune it.
level.8.hint: The higher you climb, the stronger the signal.
level.9.desc: The signal isn't coming from this world. Answer it from the ridge, then get back to camp and keep the channel open.
level.9.hint: Stand on the ridge and answer the signal.
level.10.desc: Salvage the wreck's transmitter, gather metal scrap for a reflector, assemble a beacon at camp and switch it on.
level.10.hint: Metal scrap from the wreck lies scattered along the crash furrow.
level.arc.title: Chapter Two Complete
level.arc.desc: Eleven discoveries down, and the voice in the beacon has seen them all before. Farming and metal come in a future build. Explore, trade and make more at camp.
level.arc.toast: End of Chapter One. Chapter Two starts at camp.

msg.strike1: Sparks jump into the moss… and die.
msg.strike2: A thin curl of smoke. Again.
msg.fireLit: Fire! You can see your hands again, and the dark backs off a bit.
msg.shelterBuilt: A lean-to of branches and giant fronds. It'll keep the rain off.
msg.spearCrafted: Flint lashed to a straight branch with glowvine. You feel a little less like prey.
msg.restDusk: You rest by the fire while the light fades…
msg.sleeping: You crawl into the shelter and close your eyes…
msg.houndNear: Eyes in the dark. Six of them.
msg.houndHit: The spear finds its mark. It shrieks and backs off.
msg.houndBit: It bites and darts back into the dark!
msg.houndMiss: You stab at empty air. Wait until it charges.
msg.houndFled: It's gone. For now. Sleep while you can.
msg.slept: You wake at dawn. Stiff, cold, and alive.
msg.transmitter: You dig the emergency transmitter out from under the buckled plating. Its battery still holds a charge.
msg.beaconBuilt: Tripod up, transmitter mounted, scrap panels as a reflector.
msg.crewFollow: {f:explorer} is following you. Lead the way back to camp.
msg.crewAtCamp: {f:explorer} sinks down by the fire with a long sigh.

dlg.7.1: I've got fire and a spear. My stats are kind of mid, but I'll take it. Now I wait for the dark.
dlg.8.1: A crew signal! Too weak from down here. Great. Looks like I'm doing cardio.
dlg.8.found: {f:explorer}! She's alive. But that bearing isn't on this planet. That's... that's the ring.
memory.explorer: You remember {f:explorer} on the observation deck, laughing: “If we ever crash somewhere, I'm the one who finds the way home. You just bring the snacks.”
dlg.9.1: Is someone there? {f:scientist}?! If you're a hallucination, you still owe me snacks.
dlg.9.2: I'm real. Bad news: so is the debt. Where are you?
dlg.9.3: On a rock. In the ring. My leg is cooked. And what is that stomping behind you? I'm naming it Grax.
dlg.9.4: Splint it. Whatever you've got. I watched a Tiktak about this once.
dlg.9.5: Ow! That video was not accurate! Okay. Okay. Now what?
dlg.9.6: You've got a fire going? I can hear it crackle. {f:scientist}, you might actually be a genius.
dlg.10.1: Every hull section has an emergency transmitter. Yours is buried under the plating. Dig it out, find scrap, we build a beacon. It's giving civilisation.
dlg.10.2: If anyone else survived, they'll hear it.
dlg.10.3: They're alive. All of them. {f:scientist}, they're alive!
dlg.10.4: Origin: Earth? None of us has ever even been to Earth.
dlg.10.5: That isn't a crew channel. That signal is older than our ship.

op.1: Okay besties, squad selfie, galactic core in the back. {f:strong}, chin down, your horns are photobombing.
vo.anon.op.1: Okay besties, squad selfie, galactic core in the back. Big guy, chin down, your horns are photobombing.
op.2: Bro. The horns are the aura.
op.3: Your aura just blocked the emergency exit.
op.4: Who ate my snacks? {f:scientist}. Look me in the eyes.
vo.anon.op.4: Who ate my snacks? You. Yes, you. Look me in the eyes.
op.5: Technically the snacks were communal. I have a spreadsheet.
op.6: He has a spreadsheet. We're cooked. He has been cooked since Europa.
op.7: Relax. I tightened the big window myself. It'll hold.
op.8: You said that on Ceres. That is why I carry three kinds of burn cream.
op.9: Straight on Snapgram. Caption: six lineages, one brain cell.
op.11: Me. It's always me. Which is why nobody asked how I got us this route for free.
op.12: Wait. Free? You said Lamazon Orbit had a sale.
op.13: It was lowkey a beta route. Unlisted. Slightly closer to the centre.
op.14: Bro. You booked us a side quest at a black hole.
op.15: It's an observation corridor. Perfectly safe. No cap.
op.16: You said no cap. That is how I know it's cap.
op.17: Guys. Why are the stars moving?
op.18: The nav gauge says we're drifting. We're not drifting. Gauges don't do that.
op.19: Okay. Not funny. {f:scientist}, tell me this is a prank.
vo.anon.op.19: Okay. Not funny. Tell me this is a prank.
op.20: It's not a prank. Everyone, get away from the glass.
dep.1: Day one. Six lineages, one brain cell. Say hi.
dep.3: He said he'd stay up for the launch.
dep.4: Who forgot to pack the snacks?
dep.5: Nobody forgot. You packed them. I ate them.
dep.6: You what? Okay. You owe me. It's going in the ledger.
dep.7: I packed spares. And four kinds of burn cream.
dep.8: And our sponsor. Tell them how the six of us got tickets to the galactic centre for free.

dep.10: Bro, I just want to come back with good photographs.
vo.anon.op.21: Hey! You still owe me snacks!
vo.anon.wake.line3: Hello? Squad? Anyone? Bro, even the group chat is dead.
dlg.4.1: Ancient people did this with rocks. I have two doctorates. How hard can it be.
dlg.4.3: Zero stars. Would not strike again. The survival video lied.
dlg.4.4: Fire! I am literally the main character! And nobody saw it. Of course nobody saw it.
fb.1: A memory, arriving uninvited. Day thirty-nine. The fight nobody posted.
fb.2: You're not even listening, bro. Nine days staring at that screen.
fb.3: Because the numbers are wrong, and nobody here can count past their follower count!
fb.4: Wow. Okay. Say that again, Mister Spreadsheet. Say it to my face.
fb.5: Enough. We have forty days of corridor left and one bathroom.
fb.6: He thinks he's better than us. Lab people always do.
fb.8: Hey! He's my idiot, not yours. Group hug or I'm airlocking the snacks.
fb.9: The friendship, I mean. It'll hold.
fb.10: I never said sorry. If you're out there, {f:strong}, I'm sorry.
vo.anon.fb.10: I never said sorry. If you're out there, big guy, I'm sorry.
dlg.7.2: That's six eyes. Six. Why does it need six.
dlg.7.3: Aura points: plus one thousand. I am shaking. But plus one thousand.
dlg.9.7: I thought I was the only one left.
dlg.9.8: Me too. I talked to a boulder for a whole day. Terrible listener. I'm really glad it's you.
rad.strong: Bro. Bro! Is that you? I've been losing a fight with the ground for two days. The ground is winning.
rad.medic: I have eleven minutes of light, then I sleep again. Tell {f:builder} to stop licking things.
vo.anon.rad.medic: I have eleven minutes of light, then I sleep again. Tell our builder to stop licking things.
rad.builder: Your beacon's a bit crooked. Sounds like it, I mean. But it'll hold.
rad.social: Besties! One percent battery, and I look incredible.
dlg.10.6: Wait. The beacon just dumped the liner's last log on the crew band. Course change, authorised by you. {f:scientist}, why is your name on this?
vo.anon.dlg.10.6: Wait. The liner's last log. Course change, authorised by you. Why is your name on this?
dlg.10.7: What? No. I booked a corridor. I never touched navigation.
dlg.10.8: Say it to me. No jokes. Did you bring us here on purpose?
dlg.10.9: I swear on every snack I owe you. I don't know who used my login.
dlg.10.10: Okay. I believe you. Lowkey terrified, but I believe you. So who did?
mz.intro.1: I am MegaZroN, keeper of the Last Ledger.
mz.intro.2: Six friends. One last normal day. Forty-one days later, the dark pulls them in.
mz.intro.3: Every choice you make goes in here. Let's see how it ends.
mz.l3.1: Food and sticks. The oldest speedrun in the universe, and you have finished it. Slowly.
mz.l3.red: You ate the thornix. After it tingled. I have underlined that in the Ledger. Twice.
mz.l3.safe: You examined the fruit before eating it. How disappointing. I had already sharpened my pencil.
mz.l3.died: And you have already died. Lovely. My favourite chapter is the one that restarts.
mz.l3.hint: A free hint, since you look tired. Dry moss likes open sky. You should try it.
mz.l3.2: Night is coming. Light a fire and keep it lit. You'll see why.
mz.l7.1: You survived a night. Most pages in this room stop around there, so: mild applause.
mz.l7.clean: Not one bite! That hound went home and told all six of its eyes about you.
mz.l7.bitten: It bit you. It reports that you taste of burnt coffee and poor planning.
mz.l7.2: Now listen. That dead thing on your wrist is not as dead as you think. Signals carry further in the cold, and not all of them want to be found.
mz.l7.hint: Go up. It's always uphill on this planet.
mz.ch1.1: The beacon is lit. Four friends answered. So did something that read your family tree like a menu.
mz.ch1.names: You renamed your crew. Sweet. Something down there already has their real names, and has had them for a very long time.
mz.ch1.nonames: Six names, six signals. Keep them close. Something down there collects names.
mz.ch1.2: Subjects: six. Origin: Earth. Funny, isn't it? Not one of you has ever stood on Earth. And yet you were recognised.
mz.ch1.3: Ninety-nine steps lie between you and the truth. Every one has been walked before. Check the footprints. Check the shoe size.
mz.ch1.4: See you next chapter, little traveller. I'll keep your seat warm. I always do.

codex.knapping.text: Flint breaks in smooth curved shells, not along grain. Strike the edge at the right angle and a flake comes off sharper than most knives.
codex.knapping.joke: Three million years of tech, and it's a rock hitting a rock. Same as my gym routine.
codex.cordage.text: Twist fibres and friction holds them. Twist two strands against each other and each one's urge to unwind locks the other. Short fibres become strong rope.
codex.cordage.joke: Two weak things pulling against each other and somehow getting stronger. That's literally our group chat.
codex.fire.text: Fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen. Friction heats wood dust until it smoulders into an ember. Feed it dry tinder and air, and the ember becomes flame.
codex.fire.joke: Lovely. Burns are my second favourite injury. Please stop giving me a favourite.
codex.pottery.text: Wet clay is tiny flat crystals sliding on water. Fire drives that water out of the crystals for good, so the pot can never turn back into mud. Grit in the clay stops cracks.
codex.pottery.joke: First container on the planet. Zero warranty, lopsided, no lid. Ship it.
codex.charcoal.text: Heat wood with very little air and it can't burn away. Water and gases leave, and nearly pure carbon stays. It burns far hotter and cleaner than wood.
codex.charcoal.joke: You burned wood to get better wood. I have written this in the Ledger as progress. In pencil.
codex.lime.text: Strong heat drives carbon dioxide out of limestone and leaves quicklime. Add water and it gets hot and turns to slaked lime, which slowly takes the gas back and sets like stone.
codex.lime.joke: Rock that turns to paste and back to rock. Finally, a material with my commitment issues.
codex.salt.text: Salt is dissolved in brine as charged particles. Drive off the water and they lock back into crystals. Salt keeps food by pulling out the water that microbes need.
codex.salt.joke: We're salty now. Officially. It's in the codex.
codex.glass.text: Sand melts only at huge heat, but plant ash lowers that, and lime makes the result last. Cool it fast and the atoms freeze with no time to line up. That's glass.
codex.glass.joke: Beaker first, lens later, and one day real stitches. Please don't name the first one after yourself.
codex.soap.text: An alkali from ash splits fats into soap molecules. One end loves water, the other loves oil. They wrap around grease so that water can carry it away.
codex.soap.joke: Soap has saved more lives than I ever will. I'm not crying. Go wash your hands.
codex.fermentation.text: Yeast eats sugar when there is no oxygen, and gives off alcohol and carbon dioxide. Too hot and the yeast dies. That's why a brew has to stay warm, not hot.
codex.fermentation.joke: So tiny things eat, burp and that's science? Bro, I've been a chemist my whole life.
codex.acids.text: With air, bacteria turn alcohol into sour vinegar, a weak acid. Acids give up hydrogen ions and bases take them. Mix the two and they cancel. Lichen dye shows which side you're on.
codex.acids.joke: A moss that tells you what's wrong with your drink. Finally, someone on this planet with standards.

itemdesc.limestone: Soft pale rock from the ridge.
itemdesc.brine: Salty water from a seep below the ridge.
itemdesc.ash: Pale ash raked from around the fire. Alkaline.
itemdesc.oilnut: A greasy nut. A source of fat.
itemdesc.sugarpod: Sticky sweet pod. Yeast loves it too.

itemdesc.blade: A flake with a frightening edge.
itemdesc.lime: Caustic white powder. Mortar, glass, tests.

itemdesc.glass: A cloudy lump of the first glass on this planet.

level.11.title: Cord
level.11.desc: The vine from the first night has dried and snapped. Strip bark fibre, twist real cord at camp, and set a snare.
level.11.hint: Fibre grows by the lake shore. Twist it at the fire.
level.12.title: The Stranger
level.12.desc: Check the snare. Then make a point that stays on: resin from the trees, charcoal from the fire, cord.
level.12.hint: Resin beads on broken limbs at the forest edge round camp.
level.13.title: Fire on Demand
level.13.desc: The rain put the fire out. Build a bow drill: branches, dry tinder, your cord.
level.13.hint: Dry tinder grows in the clearing. Keep the board dry under the lean-to.
level.14.title: Fire Some Clay
level.14.desc: Dig clay at the shore, temper it with sand, coil pots, and fire them through the night.
level.14.hint: Clay and sand are on the lake shore facing camp.
level.15.title: A Place to Stay
level.15.desc: The lake came up in the night. Find dry ground for a real house, and grind an axe that can cut its poles.
level.15.hint: Walk to each place the marker shows: the old camp, the reed beds, the rise by the rock shelter.
level.16.title: Posts and a Beam
level.16.desc: Six poles, a beam too heavy to lift alone and a frame that wants to fall over. Build a house that stands.
level.17.title: Wheat
level.17.desc: Oom-Sa's people grind a seed you know. Learn to make bread from it, then sow the best of it in a field by the house.
level.18.title: The Cut
level.18.desc: The wound has gone bad. Boil water, clean it, and find out what Oom-Sa's people have.
level.19.title: The Wall
level.19.desc: Meanwhile, on Methryx: Draxum builds a wall of ice blocks round his ember, and something in the lake has learnt that he is warm.
level.20.title: Water Runs Downhill
level.20.desc: Dry weeks, and the field is yellowing. Find the hill the water can run down. Then the old snare has something in it.
level.21.title: First Frost
level.21.desc: Harvest, salt, smoke and a store before the frost; the first winter storm; a stranger at dawn; and a name for the place.
level.arc2.toast: End of Chapter Two. Thank you for playing.

mg.knapping.0: Hit near the edge at a sharp angle. A blow square to the face only crushes it.
mg.cordage.0: Roll the fibres one way, lay the two strands the other. Keep it even.
mg.fire.0: Saw the bow in long even strokes until the dust smoulders.
mg.fire.1: Blow on the ember, gently. Air feeds it. Too hard and it scatters.
mg.pottery.0: Work sand into the clay. Too little grit and it cracks, too much and it crumbles.
mg.pottery.1: Bring the fire up steadily and hold it. Rush it and steam bursts the pot.
mg.charcoal.0: Keep the stack smouldering under clay. Too much air and it all burns to ash.
mg.lime.0: Hold the kiln very hot for a long time. The rock must give up its gas.
mg.lime.1: Now add water, little by little. It heats up on its own.
mg.salt.0: Warm the pot gently. You want evaporation, not a violent boil.
mg.salt.1: Stir so the crust keeps breaking and the water can leave.
mg.glass.0: Balance sand against ash and lime. The ash lowers the melting point.
mg.glass.1: The narrowest band yet. Charcoal and moving air, right at the top of what you can reach.
mg.soap.0: Balance alkali against fat. Too little and it stays greasy, too much and it stays harsh.
mg.fermentation.0: Thin the mash with water. Too sweet slows the yeast, too thin starves it.
mg.fermentation.1: Keep it warm, never hot, and leave the gas a way out.
mg.acids.0: Stir air into the mash. The vinegar bacteria need oxygen.
mg.acids.1: Add lime until the dye sits between red and blue. That is neutral.
fail.1: That was not science. That was an accident with a witness.
fail.2: Failed. I have sharpened a fresh quill for this.
fail.3: Humanity took a hundred thousand years on this. You may have five more minutes.
teach.knapping: Flint from the ridge, one hammerstone, and hit the edge, not the middle. Your rock, your fingers.
after.knapping: That's sharp. Okay, nerd. Respect. Tiny respect.
teach.cordage: Reeds at the lake. Twist one way, wrap the other. It's a friendship bracelet with consequences.
after.cordage: This cord could hold my leg together better than my splint does. Rude of it.
teach.fire: Bow, spindle, dry moss. Long strokes. No panic. I know, I'm asking a lot.
after.fire: Fire, on purpose. Our ancestors would be proud. Mine would ask why it took so long.
teach.pottery: Lake clay, some sand, then fire. Skip the sand and it pops like my knee.
after.pottery: A pot! You can carry water without crying. I'm melting mine on a hull plate, so enjoy it.
teach.charcoal: Stack wood, bury it in clay, leave a little breath. Starve it, don't kill it.
after.charcoal: Black, light, and it rings when you tap it. Next you'll say metal needs this. Right?
teach.lime: Pale rock from the ridge goes in the charcoal fire. Keep your eyes and skin far from the powder.
after.lime: You cooked a rock, and it hissed at you. Same energy as my aunt's pressure cooker.
teach.salt: That seep below your ridge, the one you said tastes like tears. Boil off the tears, keep the salt. Very therapeutic.
after.salt: Salt! Now your food might last the week. Also, tell Tovik I said he should be sweating.
teach.glass: Sand, ash, lime, charcoal, and more air than feels sensible. Stand back, then back again.
after.glass: You melted the beach and I can see through it. Okay. That one actually got me.
teach.soap: Ash water plus oilnut grease. It's the only reason I'd ever sit next to you again.
after.soap: It's ugly, it's lumpy, it smells of campfire, and I would die for it.
teach.fermentation: Mash sugarpods, keep the pot warm, and don't seal it. Trust me on not sealing it.
after.fermentation: It's bubbling by itself. Tiny roommates. They pay rent in gas.
teach.acids: Let the mash breathe till it turns sour, then balance it with lime. The lichen is the judge.
after.acids: Sour, bitter, balanced. We just did chemistry with a moss referee.
ch2.intro.1: Nobody's coming. If we want to be in one place again, we build the ship ourselves.
ch2.intro.2: Ship needs chips. Chips need glass and metal. Metal needs fire. So, rocks. We start with rocks.
ch2.intro.3: Nine ages of science, one idiot. Good luck, everybody.
ch2.beacon.pottery: Vessel. Same shape as last time.
ch2.beacon.glass: Ahead of schedule. Do not be proud.
ch2.beacon.react: Okay, that's the beacon talking. I hate that. Keep working.
ch2.end.1: Salt. Soap. Vinegar. The same order. It is always the same order.
ch2.end.2: Always? Who else has been doing this?
ch2.end.3: Next: metal. They always want metal.
ch2.end.4: It knows what we'll make before we make it. So we make something it doesn't expect.
chapter2.end2: It is always the same order

mz.ch2.clean: And you barely failed. Suspicious. Who has been helping you?
mz.ch2.messy: Yes, you ruined quite a lot of clay. It is all in here. Every lump.

mz.ch2.3: Metal next, little chemist. I have turned the page. It was already written on.

npc.trader.back: Lamazon Rock Delivery. Same day, or same century. What'll it be?
npc.trader.dead: Frequent dier! I've moved you to our premium plan. Nothing changes, but it costs more.
npc.trader.salt: You made salt? In my territory? Fine. Salt is money now. I hate how much I respect you.
npc.trader.menu: Today's catalogue. Everything is final sale, including you.
npc.trader.q: My stock smells of cave. Bring one soap and I'll pay in premium sand.
npc.trader.qdone: Five stars. I smell like a brand now. Here's your sand.

npc.local.dead: You fell down dead again. The ground says you are heavy.
npc.local.soap: You smell less loud. The ground has withdrawn its complaint.
npc.local.cord: One way for the hair, other way for the rope. Each wants to undo. Together they cannot. Like your family.
npc.local.clay: Pure clay is proud. It breaks. Give it grit. Small warm one, you could also use some.
npc.local.q: My people keep water in leaves. It is bad. Bring me one of your fire-bowls.
npc.local.qdone: Good bowl. Ugly. Good. Take this moss. It knows sour from bitter, which is more than you do.
npc.hermit.dead: You died again. Fewer times than last time. Don't let it go to your head.
npc.hermit.voice: It counts. That's all it does. I answered it once. Don't.
npc.hermit.lime: Burn it long and hot. The rock breathes out. Then water makes it scream. You always flinch at that part.
npc.hermit.glass: Charcoal alone won't do it. Move the air. Same as last time. Same as every time.
npc.hermit.soon: You always ask that before you've made it. Go and find out.
npc.trav.refund: The refund desk. It opens soon. The sign says soon. The sign has said soon for nine years.
npc.trav.dead: You died? And they let you back in? I've been asking for that upgrade for years.
npc.trav.soap: Is that soap? Amenities! I'll raise my review. To one star and a half.
npc.trav.q: A queue needs a stanchion. Bring me a clay pot and I'll give you my complimentary welcome fruit.
npc.trav.qdone: Perfect. Here, welcome fruit. It's been fizzing in my bag, so the brochure says keep it warm, not hot.

sk.dead: You keep dying and I keep doing the funeral speech. It's getting really good.

sk.done: We're out of plans for now. Make extra, trade, stay alive. I'm listening on the beacon band.
rad.ch2.strong: Ground update. It's me, one. Ground, two. Best of five. Keep working, nerd.
rad.ch2.medic: I've rationed the bandages. Wash everything. If you don't have soap yet, invent it.
rad.ch2.builder: Found a hull section. Needs welding, so you've got about four thousand years of homework.
rad.ch2.social: No signal, no followers, and something here keeps liking my posts. By that I mean it's breathing near me.
g.f.sk.dead: You keep dying and I keep doing the funeral speech. It's getting really good.

g.f.br.res.early: You answered fast. I had a whole speech ready about you being late. Wasted.
br.res.late: Took you long enough. I said goodbye to the ring twice.
br.splint.fail: Ow! The whole rock jumped and I let go. Again. Properly this time.
br.fire.ask: A big fire, and anyone else out there might see it. So might Grax. Your call.
br.fire.big.r: That's the most reckless thing you've ever said. I'm into it.
br.acc.doubt: I want to believe you. I really do. Give me a minute to actually manage it.
br.acc.proof.r: Nobody's ever just handed me the whole thing. Okay. We read it together.
br.acc.joke.r: I said no jokes. Okay. Now I know what you do when you're scared. Or when you're guilty.
g.f.br.acc.joke.r: I said no jokes. Okay. Now I know what you do when you're scared. Or when you're guilty.
br.acc.silent.r: Nothing. Okay. Nothing is an answer too.
br.fire.big: Build it up. Let them see it. Grax can leave a review.
br.fire.small: Keep it low. Staying alive first, being found second.
br.acc.proof: Here. Take the whole log. Read every line. I've got nothing to hide from you.
br.acc.joke: Obviously. I hijacked a whole liner for the free breakfast.
br.rad.medic.truth: Channel's still open. I heard all of it. Your voice never shakes when you lie. It's shaking now. So, good.
br.rad.medic.joke: Channel's still open. A joke? Right now? I'm writing that on your chart.
br.rad.medic.silent: Channel's still open. Why did you go quiet? Somebody say something.
g.f.br.rad.medic.silent: Channel's still open. Why did you go quiet? Somebody say something.
br.rad.strong.truth: Bro. If you say it wasn't you, it wasn't you. We'll find who it was. Me and the ground.
g.f.br.rad.strong.truth: Yo. If you say it wasn't you, it wasn't you. We'll find who it was. Me and the ground.
br.rad.strong.joke: Ha! Okay, that was good. Wait. Was that a yes? Bro, was that a yes?
g.f.br.rad.strong.joke: Ha! Okay, that was good. Wait. Was that a yes? Yo, was that a yes?
br.rad.strong.silent: You? Quiet? You've never been quiet in your life. Now I'm actually scared.
g.f.br.rad.strong.silent: You? Quiet? You've never been quiet in your life. Now I'm actually scared.
br.rad.builder.smoke: Loud beacon. Crooked, I can hear it. But it'll hold.
npc.trav.hungry: Nine years in this queue, and nobody has offered me so much as a biscuit.
npc.trav.fed: Is this complimentary? Five stars. I'm putting your name in the review.
npc.trav.pay: Found this in the queue. Someone dropped it in year four. It's yours now. I kept your place, too.
npc.trader.honest: You're giving it back? On this planet? I'll have to tell the rocks.
npc.trader.pay: Lamazon Rock Delivery. One vine, an order you never placed. Honest customers get the premium route.
npc.trader.short: My stock came up one flint short. Strange, that. The price is three branches now.
mz.br.truth: You told her the truth. In this room that is rarer than a quiet black hole. It won't save you, but I wrote it down.
g.f.mz.br.truth: You told her the truth. In this room that is rarer than a quiet black hole. It won't save you, but I wrote it down.
mz.br.proof: You handed her the log. All of it. I keep eleven thousand volumes, and very few people do that.
mz.br.joke: She asked you a real question and you did a bit. I laughed. She didn't. Only one of us has to live with you.
mz.br.silent: You chose to say nothing. Silence is still ink. It just dries slower.
mz.br.timeout: You let the clock answer for you. The clock has been wrong before. It never apologises.
mz.br.kind: You gave half your food to a man in a queue. Nobody saw. I see everything. It is very tiring.
mz.br.fair: You handed back a flint nobody would have missed. Strange behaviour. I've made a note.
mz.br.kept: You kept the extra flint. Small sums are how my longest books begin.
mz.br.late: {f:explorer} waited a long time for you. She won't say so twice. She doesn't have to.
mz.br.hint.pello: Someone near the second wreck is very hungry and very polite. I mention it only because I am nosy.
mz.br.hint.tovik: You are carrying something that isn't yours. It is small. Those are the ones that weigh the most.
mz.br.rec.honesty: So far your page reads honest. An inconvenient habit, out here.
mz.br.rec.mercy: So far your page reads kind. The universe hasn't noticed. I have.
mz.br.rec.nerve: So far your page reads brave. That word means foolish until the last chapter.
mz.br.rec.humour: So far your page reads funny. Every joke you make, I will read back to you at the end.
mz.br.rec.none: So far your page reads blank. Blank pages are the ones I worry about.

away.ring.intro: Tarnkin don't need air. Caravan thing. We do need water, and my leg needs a splint. Two days on a rock with a transmitter and a dish that fell off the same wall I did, and nobody has paid me back.
away.moon.shoulder: Put your shoulder back against the rock
away.wreck.bind: Bind the cut on your arm
away.clouds.ribs: Bind your ribs with your sweater
away.scree.intro: No air out here. Ortek plates seal when I hold my breath, and I can hold it a long time. Long enough to build a door, anyway.
away.wreck.intro: The lichen in my skin dried me out like seeds in a packet. I wake when the sun comes round. Eleven minutes. Then I sleep again.
away.moon.intro: Korrath don't need oxygen. We burn what Titan's sky is made of. This moon's sky is the same. It tastes like home, which is the worst part.
away.clouds.intro: Air floats in this atmosphere. So does my piece of the ship, and so do I. Fifty kilometres of cloud under me and no signal. Iconic.
away.fav.explorer: {f:explorer} marked the nearest finds on your map from up there.
away.fav.builder: {f:builder} talked you through it. Your next build won't fail.
away.fav.medic: {f:medic}'s advice worked. You feel whole again.
away.fav.strong: {f:strong}'s drills paid off. You won't tire today.
away.fav.social: {f:social}'s voice on the channel lifts everyone.

city.title: TARAVEL · 2189
away.city.intro: Boarding in one hour. I have eleven things to do and I have done zero of them.
city.task.paratha: Eat the paratha Ammi left (she will ask)
city.task.phone: Collect your phone from the Capple Store
city.task.parcel: Pick up Nuvexa's parcel at Lamazon Orbit
city.task.chai: Settle your snack debt with Skyvra at Chai Cosmos
city.task.tram: Hold the tram door while Bolzar fixes it
city.task.ring: Find Nuvexa's ring light in the square
city.task.gate: Boarding call: run to the spaceport gate
city.done.paratha: Ammi: Did you eat? Me: I am eating right now, on video, look. Ammi: Wear the jacket.
city.done.pack: Charger. Jacket, because she will ask. Snacks, because Skyvra will ask. Bag closed. Barely.
city.done.phone: Clerk: Screen, battery and a new back. That is one kidney, or two on a weekday. Me: Fine. The left one.
city.done.parcel: Locker: Parcel for Nuvexa. Contents: one travel adapter and an unreasonable amount of glitter. Have a sparkly day.
city.done.chai: Skyvra: Ledger says four samosas and a chai. Ledger has never been wrong. Me: Ledger is a menace.
city.done.tram: Bolzar: Hold it, hold it... done. It'll hold. The door slides shut, then gently falls off the other side.
city.done.ring: Found it in the fountain. Nuvexa: Don't tell anyone. Okay, tell everyone, it's content.
city.done.gate: All six of us, on time. Ammi is never going to believe this.
city.friend.strong: Draxum: I'm not crying, the holo-ad about the dog who waits for his owner is just very well made.
city.friend.medic: Lyrra: I need three kinds of burn cream. He said two is enough. He has never met Bolzar.
city.friend.explorer: Skyvra: You owe me four samosas. I'm not saying it's urgent. I'm saying it's written down.
city.friend.builder: Bolzar: Stand there. Hold that. Don't touch that. Okay, now touch it. Gently. Lowkey gently.
city.friend.social: Nuvexa: Okay, walk past me again, but like, effortlessly. No. Effortlessly. You're doing effort.
city.npc.chaiwala: Beta, chai is free. The opinions cost extra.
city.npc.aunty: So tall, so late, so single. My niece is a pilot, beta. Just saying.
city.npc.clerk: Have you tried turning your life off and on again?
city.npc.driver: Spaceport? Fixed price. Fixed by me. Today.
city.npc.kid1: Bro, that's out. That is so out. That's out in three dimensions.
city.npc.kid2: Can you bowl? You look like you can't bowl. Respectfully.
city.npc.queue1: Forty minutes in this queue. It's not a queue, it's a relationship.
city.npc.queue2: The biryani here has a waiting list. I'm on it. Spiritually.
city.npc.pharma: Your friend asked for three burn creams. I gave her two. She looked at me. I gave her three.
city.npc.tourist: Is this the real bazaar or the one for tourists? Either way I'm buying a scarf.
city.npc.mir: Third chai today. The first was for the body, the second for the soul. This one is just because the uncle looks lonely.
city.npc.mir2: Going to the galactic centre in a hoodie? Beta, at least iron it. The universe is watching.

pull.scientist: It's not a storm. Something is pulling us in, and it doesn't let go.

mz.pull.1: And that, little travellers, is what a black hole does to a holiday.
mz.pull.2: Don't look so worried. Nobody dies in the first chapter. Well. Not for long.
crew.pilot.name: Pilot
pull.pilot: Course correction. Come on. Come on.
pull.sci2: That's Sagittarius A star. It isn't pulling us in. Space is bending.
pull.pods: Everyone get to the escape pods!
pull.sci3: Nobody outside will ever see us cross. We just slow down, turn red, and fade. That stream is the last thing that got out.
mz.science: Up to the edge, that was real. Past it, nobody knows. Six guesses real physicists have made. One each.
e1.w.1: Water first. Everything else is a luxury.
e1.w.2: Downhill. Water's lazy. It always goes down.
e1.w.fail: That tasted like a swamp's armpit.
e1.w.failHint: Still water with a green skin grows what makes you sick. Moving water is safer.
e1.w.ok: Moving water. Cold. Okay. Okay. I'm alive.
e1.w.leaf: Leaf cup. Two sips' capacity. Engineering.
e1.fr.see: Something small has been eating these. So it's food. For something.
e1.fruit.title: The red fruit
e1.fr.eat: Sweet. Really sweet. Why can't I feel my tongue?
e1.fr.lyrra: “Skin, lip, tongue, then a tiny bite, then wait. If anything burns or numbs, spit and wait a day.”
e1.fr.test: {f:medic}, you nerd. You just saved my life.
e1.st.drax: “Stone talks if you tap it. Flint sings. Rubbish rock goes thunk.”
e1.stone.title: A good stone
e1.learn.goodStone: Learned: a good stone. Flint rings when you tap it.
e1.fl.hint: Strike near the edge, not the middle, and at a low angle.
e1.fl.steep: Crumbs. Too steep. Come in lower.
e1.fl.ok: Two point six million years of progress. In my hand. Bleeding.
e1.learn.flake: Learned: a stone flake. A blade.
e1.fi.sci: Friction turns work into heat. Enough heat in a pinch of wood dust and it burns by itself. That's an ember. That's all fire is: a reaction I start and then feed.
e1.fi.hint: Keep the spin in the band, then breathe the ember into the tinder.
e1.fi.slow: Smoke is not fire. Smoke is fire's trailer.
e1.fi.die: It died. Faster into the nest. Don't let it cool.
e1.fire.title: The first fire
e1.sp.drax: “Scrape it, don't chop it. Then cook the point, slow, turning, like a sausage. Dry wood is hard wood.”
e1.sp.hint: Turn the point in the coals: keep it in the band, out of the flame.
e1.sp.burn: Cooked it. Burnt it. Same thing, apparently.
e1.sh.bol: “Ridge pole first. Back to the wind. Thatch from the bottom up, like roof tiles, or the rain walks right in.”
e1.sh.wind: And the wind walks straight in. Back to the wind, he said. Turn it round.
e1.sh.thin: I can see the sky through my roof. Romantic. Bad.
e1.sh.hintWind: Put its back to the wind: mark where the wind comes from.
e1.sh.hintThatch: Lay the thatch evenly, a row at a time, from the bottom up.
e1.ts.sci: A bent stick, thrown flat, spins and sweeps a wide path. People hunted with these three hundred thousand years ago.
e1.ts.hint: Throw it flat, side-arm, as the ring closes.
e1.ts.hit: Thunk. Sorry, stump. You were practice.
e1.ts.miss: Missed. But it spun. It went the way I threw it. Mostly.
e1.vn.1: Green vine. It bends, it doesn't snap. That's a rope that grew on a tree.
e1.vn.2: A loop on a bent sapling. Stones on a line across the path. If something comes, I hear it first.
e1.learn.vines: Learned: vine traps (a snare and a rattle line).
e1.night.title: Beyond the firelight
e1.ni.held: It went away. It went away because of a stick I cooked.
e1.ni.scar: Pressure, then clean, then cover. Okay, {f:medic}. Okay.
e1.ni.hid: It walked right past me. Close enough to hear it breathe. I didn't.
e1.ni.ran: It stopped where the light starts. So the fire is the wall. Noted.
vo.anon.e1.fr.test: You nerd. You just saved my life.
vo.anon.e1.ni.scar: Pressure, then clean, then cover. Okay. Okay.

codex.haft.text: Resin softened by heat and stiffened with charcoal powder glues a stone point into a split shaft, and cord binds it. Pure resin is brittle when cold; the charcoal makes it tough. Birch tar glue at Campitello, Italy, about 200,000 years ago; hafted points at Kathu Pan, South Africa, about 500,000 years ago; plant gum and ochre glues at Sibudu, South Africa, about 70,000 years ago.
codex.haft.joke: A rock on a stick on purpose. My ancestors had a whole committee for this.
mg.haft.0: Warm the resin at the fire's edge until it softens. Too hot and it smokes and goes brittle.
mg.haft.1: Stir in crushed charcoal. Too little and it cracks in the cold, too much and it will not stick.
e2.snare.title: The snare
e2.snare.o.far: The trail down by the stream
e2.voice.title: A voice on the wind
e2.voice.ask: Someone, or something, is up on the ridge.
e2.stranger.title: The stranger
e2.stranger.ask: She has not run. Do you trust her?
e2.mark.title: The cairn
e2.mark.ask: What do you paint on it?
e2.kiln.title: The firing night
e2.kiln.ask: It is coming. The fire over the pots cannot drop.
e2.kiln.o.left: Leave the pit, hold the trail
e2.kiln.o.kept: Keep the fire, let it hold them
e2.kiln.lock: Nobody else is at the fire tonight.
e2.vn.1: Vine dries, vine snaps. One night and it's done.
e2.vn.2: Everything I want to build needs one thing tied to another. I need cord. Real cord.
e2.vn.lyrra: “Bark's inner layer, not the outside. Soak it, split it thin. Then twist one way and wrap the other, or it all just unwinds on you.”
e2.bk.1: The outer bark is armour. Under it, the part that carried water. Long fibres, all lined up.
e2.cd.fail: It unwinds. Of course it unwinds. One twist alone just wants to undo itself.
e2.cd.fix: Twist one way, wrap the other. Now each one is trying to undo the other, and that fight is what holds.
e2.cd.ok: Fifty thousand years ago someone in France did exactly this. I'm only late.
e2.sn.near: Close enough to check in the dark. Close enough for whatever checks it before me.
e2.sn.far: Further to walk. Further for anything that follows the smell.
e2.vo.1: That's me. That's... what I shouted. Yesterday.
e2.vo.go.2: Someone cut this. Someone with hands.
e2.vo.stay.2: Tired brain. Tired brain does voices.
e2.vo.high: I built that fire big so someone would see it. Someone did.
e2.st.2: You. It was you on the ridge.
e2.st.3: Small warm one. Two days you talk to yourself. Loud. I learn it.
e2.st.3h: Big fire, first night. We all saw.
e2.st.give.2: You give the meat away. You are bad at this. Good.
e2.st.sit.2: Sitting. Yes. My people also do sitting.
e2.st.joke.1: Hi. Scientist. Currently a person with a stick.
e2.st.joke.2: Person with a stick. Yes. I saw.
e2.hf.1: Cord holds it on. Cord doesn't stop it turning. I need glue.
e2.hf.oom: Tree bleeds. Sticky blood. You want this.
e2.hf.self: Resin. Trees bleed it to seal a wound. It'll seal mine.
e2.hf.burn: Burnt. It smells like a tyre. Less heat.
e2.hf.crack: Pure resin cracks in the cold. Charcoal. Charcoal makes it tough, like rebar in concrete.
e2.hf.ok: Glue, a point and a binding. People did this half a million years ago and nobody wrote it down.
e2.bd.1: It went out. All of it. And my hands remember the hand drill.
e2.bd.2: But I have cord now. A bow turns a push into a spin. Same friction, a tenth of the work.
e2.bd.slip: Too loose. It's slipping. Tighter, so it bites.
e2.bd.jump: Press down. The stone holds the top so the bottom has to work.
e2.bd.ok: Fire. On purpose. In a minute. That's not luck any more, that's a method.
e2.py.2: Pyrite. Iron and sulfur. The sparks are the pyrite burning in the air. Neanderthals did that.
e2.rs.1: That's my flake. That's... the same flake.
e2.rs.2: Same stone, same physics, same answer. Anyone who works it out gets this shape. That's all it is.
e2.rs.3: But this took thousands of years to go white.
e2.mk.one: Me, and how long. If anyone comes, they'll know how long I waited.
e2.cl.1: Clay. Tiny flat crystals with water between them. Wet, they slide. Fired, they fuse into stone you shaped yourself.
e2.cl.bolzar: “Grit in the mix, mate. Pure stuff cracks when it shrinks. Grit lets it breathe.”
e2.cl.crack: Too fast. The outside dried and shrank and the inside didn't. Slow. Slow.
e2.fr.1: Slow first. Any water left inside turns to steam, and the steam wants out.
e2.fr.2: Then hot, and hotter, and keep it there. All night.
e2.fr.oom: Big one walks tonight. It smells your fire. It remembers you.
e2.fr.look: It looked at me. It looked at me like it knew my face.
e2.dw.1: It rings. No crack. Same test as the stones.
e2.dw.lost: Not all of them. Enough to learn on.
e2.dw.2: Boiled water. {f:medic} would cry. Then she'd tell me to boil it longer.
e2.dw.3: First pot on this whole world. I think.
e2.dw.oom: Fire-bowl. My people keep water in leaves. It is bad.
e2.mz.1: Day ten. Cord, glue, a spark on purpose, and a pot that rings. He has invented the kitchen.
g.f.e2.mz.1: Day ten. Cord, glue, a spark on purpose, and a pot that rings. She has invented the kitchen.
e2.mz.kind: And he met someone, and gave them his time. That is the other invention. It takes longer.
g.f.e2.mz.kind: And she met someone, and gave them her time. That is the other invention. It takes longer.
e2.mz.spear: And he met someone, and pointed a stick at her. She wrote it down too. They all do.
g.f.e2.mz.spear: And she met someone, and pointed a stick at her. She wrote it down too. They all do.
e2.mz.none: And he met someone, and said nothing at all. I have a whole shelf of those.
g.f.e2.mz.none: And she met someone, and said nothing at all. I have a whole shelf of those.
e2.mz.cairn: He built a pile of stones for people he does not know are alive. I have read that page before. It never gets less stupid. It never gets less right.
g.f.e2.mz.cairn: She built a pile of stones for people she does not know are alive. I have read that page before. It never gets less stupid. It never gets less right.
e2.mz.bare: He stacked the stones and left them blank. Honest. Nobody would know who to come back for.
g.f.e2.mz.bare: She stacked the stones and left them blank. Honest. Nobody would know who to come back for.
e2.mz.4: Next, he wants to stay somewhere. Places are harder than pots.
g.f.e2.mz.4: Next, she wants to stay somewhere. Places are harder than pots.
vo.anon.e2.dw.2: Boiled water. Our medic would cry. Then she'd tell me to boil it longer.

e2.cordAgain: You twist another cord from the fibre you kept.

e3.obj.site: Look at where you could build ({n} of 3 seen)
e3.obj.axe: Cut poles: try the sapling at the forest edge
level.15.hint2: Two stones and sand from the shore: grind an axe head at camp.
e3.fl.1: Lean-to. The name says it. It leans. It's not a house.
e3.fl.2: I've got a pot that rings and nowhere to put it. If I'm staying, I'm staying properly.
e3.fl.bolzar: “First thing, mate: where the water goes when it rains a lot. Then build where it doesn't.”
e3.fl.rise: Dry. High. Far from water, far from her people. Close to the old hands on the wall.
e3.fl.reeds: Flat, soft, near the reeds. Near them.
e3.fl.reeds.low: They watch me from the reeds. They'll move if I build here.
e3.fl.camp: Raise the floor. Ditch round it. I know this place.
e3.site.title: Where to build
e3.site.ask: Where do you build the house?
e3.site.o.rise: The rise by the rock shelter
e3.site.o.reeds: By the reeds, near her people
e3.st.rise: Dry and high. I'll carry water. Water's lighter than a flood.
e3.st.reeds: Near them. If they'll have me near them.
e3.st.camp: Here. A raised floor and a ditch round it. I know this place.
e3.ax.1: Chipped edges are sharp and they snap. I need an edge that lasts. That means grinding.
e3.ax.drax: “Don't hit it to make it sharp. Hit it to make it the shape. Grind it to make it sharp.”
e3.ax.rhythm: Long strokes. Even. Rushing it just scratches.
e3.ax.dry: Dry, it clogs and chips. Wet it. The water carries the sand and the heat off.
e3.ax.wet: Too wet. The sand's gone. It's just rubbing.
e3.ax.ok: Four strokes. The chipped one took forty. Ten thousand years ago this is what cleared forests.
e3.obj.ditch: Dig a ditch round the floor at the old camp
e3.obj.frame: Build the frame at the place you chose
e3.fr.1: Posts in the ground, a beam on top, rafters off the beam. Every barn on Earth for ten thousand years.
e3.fr.bolzar: “Post goes a third into the ground or it walks. And a box wants to fall over sideways. Triangles don't.”
e3.fr.ditch: Round the floor and out to the low side. The rain goes round the house, not through it.
e3.fr.tap: Loose. A post in loose earth walks. Pack it in layers, stones and all.
e3.fr.lever: Slow. Rush it and it slides off the chocks. A hand at a time.
e3.fr.fail: It's a parallelogram. Push it and it folds. Of course it does.
e3.fr.fix: A diagonal, corner to corner. Now it's two triangles, and a triangle can't change shape without breaking a side.
e3.fr.thatch: Bottom row first, each row over the one below. Rain runs down the top layer and never finds the inside.
e3.fr.slip: Knot. The axe came off it into my arm. Brilliant.
e3.fr.bind: Bark and cord. It's a cut. I've had worse.
e3.dr.bolzar: “The wind side is the back, mate. Always the back.”
e3.door.title: The door
e3.door.ask: Which way does the door face?
e3.door.o.view: Towards the lake. For the view.
e3.dr.lee: Back to the wind off the lake. Whatever it throws hits a wall, not the door.
e3.dr.band: Facing them. They'll see my fire at night. I'll see theirs.
e3.dr.joke: Morning sun, water, the giant coming up. If I'm going to be stuck here, I'm going to be stuck here with a view.
e3.learn.frame: Learned: posts and a beam, the lever and the brace
codex.polish.text: A stone head roughed out by knapping, then ground for hours on a flat stone with wet sand, gets a smooth edge that bites into green wood and does not chip. The water carries the sand and the heat. Ground axes cleared the forests of the Neolithic Near East and Europe from about 10,000 years ago; ground-edge axes in Arnhem Land, Australia, are about 44,000 to 49,000 years old, and in Japan about 38,000.
codex.polish.joke: Three days of rubbing a rock for four seconds of chopping. Agriculture is going to be worse.
mg.polish.0: Push the head along the wet stone in long, even strokes.
mg.polish.1: Sand and water on the stone. Too dry and it clogs and chips, too wet and the sand washes off.
mg.frame.0: Ram each post down a third of its length. Hit it square, or it leans.
mg.frame.1: Lever the beam up a hand at a time. Push on the long end, steady, or it slips off the log.
mg.grain.0: Push the hand stone over the grain in long strokes. Too fast and it skips, too slow and it clogs.
mg.grain.1: The flat stone in the fire: hot enough to bake, not so hot it burns.
mg.farming.0: Press each seed in two knuckles deep.
mg.farming.1: Open the row with the digging stick in steady strokes.
mg.remedy.0: Bring the water to a rolling boil and keep it there. Too cool is not clean, too hard boils over.
mg.remedy.1: Clean the wound out in slow strokes with the lichen. Rush it and it is not clean.
mg.icewall.0: Score the ice along a line with the stone, square each time.
mg.icewall.1: Lever the block out with the pole, slow and steady.
mg.irrigation.0: Peg the ditch with the A-frame so it falls a hand every few paces.
mg.irrigation.1: Dig along the pegs and throw the soil on the low side.
codex.frame.text: Posts set a third of their length into the ground, a ridge beam lifted with a lever, rafters, a diagonal brace (a frame of triangles cannot fold), thatch laid from the eaves up. Post-built houses at Ohalo II, Israel, about 23,000 years ago; the longhouses of Neolithic Europe.
codex.frame.joke: A box falls over, mate. I told you. Triangles.
codex.remedy.text: Boiled water to clean a wound, the dead tissue cut away, honey on it (its sugar draws water out of bacteria and it slowly makes hydrogen peroxide), a lichen with an antibacterial acid. Honey on wounds in the Edwin Smith papyrus, Egypt, about 1600 BCE; Sushruta's surgery, India, about 600 BCE.
codex.remedy.joke: Honey: the only medicine that stings you before you get it.
codex.icewall.text: At minus 180 C water ice is as hard as rock: on Methryx a lake is a quarry. Blocks scored and levered out, laid in courses.
codex.icewall.joke: Draxum's review of the moon's building materials: rock, rock, rock that melts if you love it.
level.16.hint: Gather branches and reed fibre, then build the frame where you chose to live.
level.17.hint: Sow the biggest seed in rows at the field beside the house.

e3.learn.grain: Learned: grinding grain and baking flatbread
e3.learn.farming: Learned: saving seed and sowing a field
e3.l17.oom: She wants me to follow her. All right. I'm coming.
e3.l17.wk: The small one from the reeds. He wants me to follow him.
e3.hm.1: You are the loud one. Fire, first night.
e3.hm.1h: The big fire. The first night. We sat on the hill and watched you not sleep.
e3.hm.cairn: Your stones on the hill. Six marks. We put one more. For you.
e3.hm.2: We gather. Grass gives, we take. You will do the strange thing.
e3.wh.2: Not like wheat. Not wheat-ish. Emmer. Wild emmer. On a planet in another universe.
e3.wh.3: Convergent evolution doesn't do this. It does wings and eyes. It doesn't do the crease.
e3.gr.grit: Grit. The stone's grinding itself into the flour. Teeth won't thank me. Harder stone.
e3.gr.rhythm: Down the hollow and back. Steady. Jerking it just throws the grain out.
e3.gr.burnt: Black. Too hot. That's charcoal with ambitions.
e3.gr.dough: Still dough. The stone's not hot enough. Push it nearer the fire.
e3.gr.ok: Bread. Fourteen thousand years ago somebody did this and cried, probably.
e3.fd.1: Save the biggest seed. Plant it. Save the biggest from that. Do it for a few hundred years and you've got farming. I'll do it for one.
e3.fd.lyrra: “Seeds want to be just under, not buried. Two knuckles deep. Any deeper and they run out of themselves before they find the light.”
e3.fd.deep: Too deep. They'll run out of themselves before they find the light. Two knuckles.
e3.fd.shallow: Too shallow. That's not sowing, that's feeding the birds.
e3.fd.rows: Straight rows. If I can't walk between them I can't weed them.
e3.field.title: The seed
e3.field.ask: The field is sown with the best of it. What about the rest of the seed?
e3.field.o.band: Give half to the band to plant.
e3.fd.all: All of it, then. A big field or nothing. The weather gets a vote.
e3.fd.half: Half in the ground, half in the pot. If the field fails I still eat in the winter.
e3.fd.band: Half for them. They'll think I'm mad. A field each is twice the chance.
codex.grain.text: Wild grain ground between a hollowed stone and a hand stone, the flour mixed with water and baked on a hot flat stone. People ground wild grain at Ohalo II, Israel, about 23,000 years ago, and baked flatbread at Shubayqa 1, Jordan, about 14,400 years ago, before anyone farmed.
codex.grain.joke: The first bread had sand in it. So did the second. Archaeologists can tell from the teeth.
codex.farming.text: Saving the biggest seed and sowing it, year after year, slowly turns a wild grass into a crop. Farming began in the Fertile Crescent about 11,500 years ago with emmer, einkorn and barley, and on its own in China (rice, millet), New Guinea, Mesoamerica (maize), the Andes and West Africa.
codex.farming.joke: Humans: stopped walking after food, started walking behind it in straight lines.
level.18.hint: Boil water in your pot at the fire, with lichen from the forest edge.
e3.obj.lichen: Find lichen at the forest edge
e3.obj.boil: Boil water at the fire and clean the wound
e3.learn.remedy: Learned: boiling water and cleaning a wound
e3.ct.1: That's the infection walking up the lymph. That's a hospital, on Earth. That's a drip and a nurse who's annoyed with me.
e3.ct.2: Here it's a pot and a fire and me.
e3.ct.lyrra: “Boil the water first. Clean it out, all of it, even when it hurts, especially when it hurts. Honey on it, if you can get honey. And don't be brave about it.”
e3.ct.usnea: This lichen. Lyrra showed me one like it. There's an acid in it that bacteria hate.
e3.ct.cool: Not boiling. Warm water is soup for whatever lives in it. Hotter.
e3.ct.over: Boiled over. Half the pot's in the fire. Not so hard.
e3.ct.rush: Too fast. Clean it out, all of it. Even when it hurts.
e3.ct.ok: Boiled, cooled, cleaned as well as I can. It's not enough. It's still walking up the arm.
e3.ds.1: Sweet-wax heals. We have this much. The small one has the hot sickness too.
e3.ds.2: That's enough for one of us. Properly. Not two.
e3.dose.title: The one dose
e3.dose.o.self: I take it. I'm the one who can make the next thing.
e3.ds.boy: It's his. Hold him still. This is going to sting.
e3.ds.truth: If I die the field dies, the house, all of it. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, and I'm right.
e3.ds.half: Half each. It's not enough for either of us. It's what there is.
e3.ds.carried: Three days. You were heavy. The small one held your hand.
e3.ds.alone: Three days. On my own floor. I don't remember getting here.
e3.ds.end: Boiled water and honey. Lyrra would say I left it two days too long. Lyrra would be right.
level.19.hint: Haul the ice blocks to the ring round the ember.
e3.dx.1: Water ice at minus one-eighty is rock. Good rock. I've got a whole lake of bricks.
e3.dx.melt: Hot hands. Of course. I'm a heater. It slumps where I hold it. Wrap them.
e3.dx.wrap: Sleeves round the palms. Torn jacket, best gloves on the moon.
e3.dx.why: Something to guard, welder. A man needs something to guard.
e3.dx.hum: It'll hold. It'll hold. It'll hold.
e3.dx.knows: That's not him. That's you. You learnt him off the wind.
e3.dx.ring: Half a circle. Waist high. Round nothing. Good.
e3.dx.come: Something's coming out of the lake. Long. The colour of the slush.
e3.wall.title: The wall
e3.wall.ask: It wants into the ring. It has learnt that you are warm.
e3.wall.o.climb: Up the cliff. Let it have the ring.
e3.dx.mocked: Didn't like that, did you. Your own trick, back at you. Go on.
e3.dx.lost: Thirty days of blocks. Fine. Plenty of lake.
e3.dx.held: Back under the ice. Good. The wall held. I held.
e3.dx.thrown: Threw me like a sack. It's gone. I'm still here. That's a win, on Methryx.
e3.dx.end: Start again in the morning. Something to guard.
level.20.hint: Make an A-frame level at the field: three branches and a stone.
e3.dry: Day {n}. No rain for nine days.
e3.obj.level: Peg a ditch from the stream to the field
e3.learn.irrigation: Learned: a ditch that falls just enough
e3.ir.1: Water runs downhill. That's the whole of irrigation. The rest is finding the hill.
e3.ir.rise: The stream's below me. Water doesn't run up. Take it from further up, where it's higher than the field.
e3.ir.steep: Too steep. It's eating its own bed. Shallower.
e3.ir.flat: Flat. It's just a long puddle now.
e3.ir.dig: Soil out on the low side, or the first rain puts it all back.
e3.ir.ok: Look at it go. Six thousand years ago in Mesopotamia somebody did this and became a king.
e3.kt.1: Baby. You're a baby. Your mother's gone, and I'm hungry, and you're a baby.
e3.kt.fed: I fed one of these once. A different one. It looked at me the same.
e3.kt.killed: Last time I did the sensible thing. I still hear it.
e3.kit.title: The kit
e3.kit.ask: A young nibbet in the snare, alive. What do you do?
e3.kt.keep: Come on, then. You live at mine now. Don't eat the field.
e3.kt.free: Go on. Grow up somewhere else.
e3.kt.eat: I'm sorry. I'm hungry, and I'm sorry.
codex.irrigation.text: Water led from a river along ditches that fall just enough to keep it moving. Irrigation fed Mesopotamia's cities from about 6000 BCE; the Egyptians and Romans laid out the fall with an A-frame level (a plumb line against a mark on the crossbar), Persia dug qanats under the desert and the Indus cities drained their streets.
codex.irrigation.joke: Bolzar's whole philosophy of civil engineering: find out where the water wants to go, then pretend it was your idea.
level.21.hint: Boil brine down in your pot at the hearth: three scoops from the seep below the ridge.
e3.obj.salt: Boil the brine down at the hearth
e3.obj.brine: Fetch brine from the seep below the ridge
e3.learn.store: Learned: salt, smoking, a store and a tally
e3.hv.1: Wind does the sorting. Grain's heavy, chaff isn't.
e3.ct.nuvexa: “If you don't count it, it isn't yours. It's just a pile.”
e3.tl.1: A tally stick. The Lebombo bone has twenty-nine notches and it's forty-three thousand years old. I'm in good company.
e3.tr.1: It came to look. It always comes to look.
e3.sa.spit: Too hard. It spits, and the pot will crack. Slow.
e3.sa.slow: Barely steaming. At this rate it's salt by the spring.
e3.sa.scrape: Gently. Scrape the crust, not the pot.
e3.sm.lee: The wind's on the back wall. The door's quiet. Good call, Bolzar.
e3.sm.view: The wind's coming straight off the lake. At the door. Of course it is.
e3.sm.band: The wind's on the door side. Hold it.
e3.sm.flood: Water under the door. The floor's going. I should have dug the ditch.
e3.sm.kit: The kit's squealing. Something's out there. Something's come for the store.
e3.st.1: Eleven people in a house for one. That's not a house any more. That's a village.
crew.pello.name: Pello
e3.pl.1: Excuse me. Is this the queue? For the refunds?
e3.pl.3: I've been waiting nine years. Nobody's called my number.
e3.pl.oom: The waiting man. He walks. He waits. We give him fish.
e3.pello.title: The man with the ticket
e3.pello.ask: He stands at the edge of the light, swaying.
e3.pl.ask: The Second Sun. Economy. We came through the dark, all of us. Then I was here and they weren't.
e3.pl.in: Come in. There's a fire. There's bread, sort of.
e3.pl.out: Not here. Keep walking. I'm sorry.
e3.pl.end: Nine years. Another ship. Through the same dark.
e3.name.title: A name
e3.name.ask: Smoke from the roof hole, frost on the thatch. What is this place called?
e3.name.o.hatum: Ha-Tum, Hoh-Ma's word: the place that stays.
e3.nm.1: A place. Mine. Theirs. Ours, maybe.
e3.mz.1: Day eighty. A house, a field, a ditch, a pot of salt, a stick with notches in it. He has invented the village. It always looks smaller than it is.
e3.mz.boy: He gave the honey to the child and nearly died of being right.
e3.mz.self: He kept the honey and lived and was right, and the child limps. I wrote both down. I always write both down.
e3.mz.half: He cut the medicine in half. Medicine does not like being cut in half. Neither do people.
e3.mz.wall: Somewhere very cold, a man built a wall to have something to guard.
e3.mz.pello: And a man came out of the storm with a ticket. I have his page too. It is a long page.
e3.mz.4: Next, he has to remember things longer than he can remember them. Marks on clay.
